newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE aims to be centre of euro derivatives trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE aims to be centre of euro derivatives trade.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Wednesday it aimed to be the centre for world euro derivatives trade and its new Bobl contracts represented a step towards that.

"LIFFE's stated ambition is to be the centre for world euro derivatives trading after EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union) and the launch of its Bobl contracts is one more step to achieving this ambition," LIFFE chief executive Daniel Hodson said in a statement.
The launch substantially strengthens LIFFE's product range in the runup to EMU, LIFFE said.
"LIFFE already has the dominant position in both benchmark deutschemark products, the Bund and the three-month Euromark," Hodson said.

"Now it is launching Bobl futures and options for which there is strong member and market demand, resulting from the rapid growth and internationalistation of the five-year section of the deutschemark yield curve," he said.
He said LIFFE will have guaranteed liquidity for its two new Bobl contracts as part of designated market making schemes which it is introducing as part of the launch.
-- is open for all members to apply to act as designated market markers in either Bobl futures, Bobl options, or both, through a competitive bidding process,
-- requires a commitment to provide, at least, a maximum bid/offer spread of two ticks in a minimum size of at least 200 lots in the most actively traded futures contract month,
-- provides trade sharing privileges for designated market makers, and financial benefits linked to the contracts' success,
-- and has one member prepared to commit on the terms set out.
